task.name: An unversioned alias is the routing candidate, so evidence accrues to a moving target and earlier versions cannot be offered as alternatives
task.story_text:
## Why

A routing candidate is currently allowed to be a model family rather than a model. Some catalog
entries name an unversioned vendor alias, which the vendor resolves at invocation time to whichever
concrete version it currently ships. The candidate the router reasons about, the identity recorded
against the run, and the accumulated evidence are all keyed to the alias, not to what actually ran.

This has two consequences, and the second is easy to miss.

**Evidence accrues to a moving target.** Observations gathered under an alias describe whatever the
alias meant at the time. When the vendor advances it, the history continues accumulating under the
same key as though the subject were unchanged. A consumer applying a sample floor, a recency
weighting, or a cost cohort to that history is treating observations of two different models as
observations of one, and nothing marks the discontinuity.

**Earlier versions cannot be offered as alternatives.** An alias can only mean the current release,
so a previous generation is not expressible as a candidate at all — even when it is cheaper, and
even when it is sufficient for the work being routed. This is not hypothetical: a single provider
currently serves more than forty models spanning several generations at materially different price
points, and the catalog can name only the newest of each family. A router whose purpose is choosing
among candidates on evidence cannot choose a candidate it has no way to name, so the entire
cost-versus-capability tradeoff across generations is unavailable by construction.

Aliases are still worth having. Tracking a family's current release is a reasonable default and is
why one provider's entries stayed current here while another's fell two generations behind. The
defect is that an alias is currently the *only* thing expressible for those families, and that what
it resolved to is neither recorded nor available to reason about.

## Acceptance criteria

- A specific model version is expressible as a routing candidate for any provider that publishes
  versions, alongside — not instead of — the family alias.
- Where a candidate names a family rather than a version, the version that served is recorded
  against the run and is distinguishable from the family name that selected it.
- Evidence accumulated for a family alias is attributable to the versions that produced it, so a
  consumer can tell whether a population describes one model or several.
- A change in what an alias resolves to is detectable from recorded runs rather than only from a
  behavioural surprise.
- Nothing requires an operator to pin a version: a configuration naming only aliases keeps working
  and keeps tracking current releases.

## Example

What the catalog can express today versus what the provider actually serves:

```
catalog can name        opus                    (whatever ships today)
                        sonnet                  (whatever ships today)

provider serves         claude-opus-5           $5 / $25
                        claude-opus-4-8         $5 / $25
                        claude-haiku-4-5        $1 / $5
                        ...and further versions per family

recorded against runs   anthropic/opus/cli      the alias — the version is not the identity
```

A run that used the alias records the alias. If the alias advances a generation, the next run
records the same identity for a different model, and the two are indistinguishable in the history
that routing consumes.

Depends on #2252

handoff.summary: Iteration 1 fixes three P1 findings, all the same shape — version-level evidence attributed to the wrong invocation. (1) agent_identity._record_ledgers double-counted every ordinary preflight: preflight.attempts records EVERY attempt including the final one, and that final attempt is what becomes state.preflight_result and therefore the cost.agents preflight entry, so the two record surfaces overlap by exactly one entry and alias-drift counted it twice. The last attempt is now skipped when its ledger signature matches a cost.agents preflight ledger, via a new _ledger_signature helper. The rule is positional AND signature-confirmed rather than signature-only, because both simpler rules are wrong: a same-profile parse retry resolves to the same version as the attempt it replaced (signature-only would erase a real invocation), and a record whose preflight result never reached cost.agents has nothing to duplicate (positional-only would drop it). (2) Reviewer value samples were stamped by a name-only newest-wins join in the bridge, so a reviewer served by different versions across plan-review attempts or code-review cycles had every sample labelled with the newest version. resolved_model is now captured on each telemetry row at source by the pool that ran the invocation — plan_flow uses pr_results[_i], review_pool uses successful[_i], both index-aligned with the profile list — and _resolved_by_reviewer is deleted rather than patched. (3) _update_review folded the cycle-denominated findings/cost aggregate under a single served version. RunOutcome.reviewer_resolved_cycles now carries a per-reviewer {served identity: cycles} map built by _review_resolved_cycle_counts, joined per (reviewer, cycle) against the reviewer-attempt records, and _update_review takes resolved_cycles and folds each version with its own cycle count. A parse retry inside one cycle stays one cycle of evidence; cycles whose attempt recorded no identity are absent, so the breakdown under-claims rather than over-claims and can never sum past the counter it explains. Pattern sweep: _record_ledgers was the only reader of two record surfaces (dev_identity_ledger and dev_model_identity_detail read cost.agents alone); the only other name-keyed reviewer join is _rev_identity in apply_run, which maps to the configured profile identity and genuinely does not vary per cycle, so it stays. Also corrected the stale 'only the final attempt reaches cost.agents' framing in ADR-0002 and in the _invocation_identity_params docstring, both written from the same wrong assumption in iteration 0.

handoff.summary: Iteration 1 fixes the two cycle-2 P1s, both in the code-review parse-retry path. A retry supersedes the initial invocation's output and can be served by a different concrete version; two consumers still followed the superseded invocation. (1) review_pool now maintains _results_for_parsed — the AgentResult backing each reviewer's FINAL parsed output — initialised to list(successful) and updated in lockstep with parsed_results whenever a retry succeeds. The code-reviewer value sample reads _results_for_parsed[_i] instead of successful[_i], so the sample names the model that produced the findings it measures. (2) Cycle attribution moved onto the cycle itself rather than being patched in the scan. ReviewCycleMetadata gains resolved_by_reviewer, populated from the same _results_for_parsed list at the end of the pool, and _review_resolved_cycle_counts reads it instead of scanning state.reviewer_attempts. The attempt log holds every invocation including superseded ones and cannot express which output the cycle used; worse, retries are appended BEFORE the initial record, so the previous last-wins rule selected the superseded version in every retry case. _extract_reviewers and _review_resolved_cycle_counts now iterate the same meta.successful participants, so the cycle count and its version breakdown derive from one source and cannot disagree. Pattern check: the analogous plan-review path was read, not assumed — _retry_parse_failed_plan_reviews already returns retried_results with the surviving result per index and pr_results is reassigned from it before the value loop, so plan_flow needed no change; _original_result = successful[i] inside the retry loop is correct as-is (prompt anchor and session id, deliberately the original). Beyond the findings, per convention 6: reviews[*].resolved_by_reviewer is now written into the audit record, because per-cycle attribution is exactly the value that cannot be reconstructed from the per-invocation entries — the gap that made this bug possible. ADR-0002 records the reasoning. Nothing else from prior iterations changed: the catalog, the substrate schema, the two scoped breakdown keys, the preflight de-duplication and the alias_derived projection are untouched.

findings.description: For a normal preflight record, the final preflight invocation is read from both cost.agents and preflight.attempts, so invocation_identity_rows emits two identity rows for the same invocation and alias-drift overcounts it.

When a reviewer profile participates in multiple review cycles that served different versions, the cycle-denominated review findings and cost population is folded under only one resolved version.

plan_review.findings:
- [P1-impl] [anthropic-opus-cli] Step 2 changes canonical_id_for_legacy_key semantics but does not list src/theforge/cli/profiles.py:134, which calls it in the profiles-migration display path, nor model_profiles.py:2833/2910 migration callsites beyond the named tests. The signature is unchanged so nothing breaks at import, but a key that previously folded to anthropic/sonnet/cli and now resolves to a pinned id (or stays unresolved) will change what forge profiles migration reports.
  Suggestion: While implementing Step 2, check the three existing callsites and confirm the migration/report path treats a newly-pinned canonical id and a still-unresolved key correctly rather than as an ambiguity regression.
- [P1-impl] [anthropic-opus-cli] Step 1 does not state how the new pinned Anthropic entries satisfy the catalog's attribution rules — cost_rank_basis must be stated whenever the band is not the entry's own attributable price band, and an unstated, underivable band is a load error (models.yaml header, config/pricing.py, model_duplicates._ROUTING_READS).
  Suggestion: Pin the concrete entries with pricing_provenance naming the billed identity (PRICING_TABLE already carries claude-opus-4-6 and claude-sonnet-4-6) so their bands derive from their own attributable prices; only fall back to cost_rank_basis where a price cannot be attributed.
- [P1-impl] [anthropic-opus-cli] Step 4 folds the same admissible run into both the configured alias bucket and the resolved concrete model's profile entry. Aggregate counts across candidates (sample floors applied fleet-wide, cost cohorts, any 'total observations' read) can now see one run twice.
  Suggestion: Keep per-candidate counts authoritative and mark alias-derived evidence on the concrete entry so any cross-candidate aggregation can exclude the duplicate projection.
- [P2] [anthropic-opus-cli] Step 3 bumps SUBSTRATE_SCHEMA_VERSION (currently 7, the DB-schema counter) while a separate per-record migration chain exists up to _migrate_v9_to_v10 in the same module. The plan does not say which counter it means.
  Suggestion: Confirm the new table is a DB-schema change only (SUBSTRATE_SCHEMA_VERSION + _MIGRATIONS list + a reindex helper modeled on _reindex_dev_model_identity) and that no record-level MIGRATION_HELPERS entry is implied.
- [P2] [anthropic-opus-cli] Preflight named src/theforge/config/model_catalog.py and model_identity.py as likely files; Step 1 lists config/models.py instead. This is probably correct (the catalog is data-driven and models.py owns AGENT_REGISTRY/known_raw_model_key_prefixes), but the parser may still need to accept a pinned entry beside an alias of the same family.
  Suggestion: If load_packaged_catalog or the duplicate/identity checks reject two same-provider entries in the same family, extend model_catalog.py rather than working around it in the data file.
- [P1-impl] [openai-gpt-5.4-cli] Step 3 says the new role-neutral invocation index will be populated from cost.agents, but not every recorded invocation lives there today: earlier preflight retry/fallback attempts are recorded only under preflight.attempts[*].ledger (src/theforge/coordinator/preflight_flow.py, src/theforge/coordinator/audit_render.py). If the intended contract is truly 'every recorded invocation', limiting the index to cost.agents would miss that path.
  Suggestion: Either include preflight.attempts[*].ledger in the new index, or narrow the step/CLI contract to top-level cost.agents invocations so the implementation and operator surface stay truthful.
- [P1-impl] [openai-gpt-5.4-cli] Steps 4-5 describe version-aware profile evidence, but assignment.py routes from .forge/model_profiles.yaml, and the current update path (src/theforge/model_profiles.py:update_from_run) only appends new runs. There is no existing rebuild-from-audit path for historical profile aggregates, so previously mixed alias history would stay opaque unless the implementation adds one.
  Suggestion: Add an explicit migration/backfill decision in src/theforge/model_profiles.py (and, if needed, src/theforge/cli/migrate_profiles.py): either rebuild/populate the new resolved-version breakdown from recorded audit ledgers, or surface legacy pre-breakdown populations as explicitly unknown/mixed until fresh runs refill them.
- [P2] [openai-gpt-5.4-cli] Step 4 relies on resolved identity reaching all reviewer-value evidence, but the native plan-review value capture currently writes only profile identity fields into state.plan_reviewer_value (src/theforge/coordinator/plan_flow.py), unlike cost.agents ledgers.
  Suggestion: During implementation, either add resolved/configured identity capture to the plan-review value rows in plan_flow.py or document and implement a deterministic join in model_profiles_bridge.py against state.plan_review_results so plan-review value samples can be attributed to concrete served versions.

finding_registry.description: For a normal preflight record, the final preflight invocation is read from both cost.agents and preflight.attempts, so invocation_identity_rows emits two identity rows for the same invocation and alias-drift overcounts it.

When the same reviewer profile has value samples from multiple plan-review attempts or code-review cycles that resolved to different versions, every sample is stamped with the newest resolved version for that reviewer.
When a reviewer profile participates in multiple review cycles that served different versions, the cycle-denominated review findings and cost population is folded under only one resolved version.
When a code reviewer has an unparseable initial invocation under one resolved version and a parse retry succeeds under another, the review cycle is attributed to the superseded initial version.
When a code-review parse retry replaces a reviewers parsed output, the value sample for the retry output is stamped with the resolved version from the original transport-success result.

soft: Coordinator is pure Python — no LLM calls for routing or process decisions
Schema validation is the integrity boundary — do not relax cross-validation rules
Keep modules single-purpose; extract instead of growing monolith files
Keep pure-data types in low-dependency modules with stdlib-only imports
Separate prompt construction, output parsing, and coordinator control flow

When adding or modifying data that flows between coordinator phases, instrument the change so the actual values are visible in the audit trail — diagnosing sprint failures requires tracing real data, not reconstructing it
Do not create files outside src/, tests/, or docs/. If you need a scratch file for exploration, delete it before committing.

Changes that affect coordinator phase boundaries, state handoff between phases, or adaptive routing/config propagation must include seam-level integration tests covering the touched boundary. Unit tests alone are insufficient when correctness depends on cross-phase state flow.
